pages: A small boy of about six, dark hair, a brown knit jersey with a hole at the elbow, standing on the mill landing with one hand on the rail, looking down at the water. Middle distance: the mill wheel, the low weir. Background: the mill on the Wen at Tarbeck, late afternoon. Light: low sun on the wheel, blue shade in the race.

A young man of about nineteen, dark hair, a scarlet moleskin work coat with the sleeves pushed back, holding a small round tin up in his open palm and looking down at it. Middle distance: a drawer standing open, a folded cloth. Background: the mill kitchen at Tarbeck, morning. Light: low sun through one small window.

Roon Vail, nineteen, dark wet hair, a scarlet moleskin work coat soaked to the shoulder, bent over the weir with one bare arm in the water and his hand closing on something solid. Middle distance: matted weed on the boards, a black horn comb on his open palm. Background: the low weir on the Wen, no moon. Light: a lantern on the boards, blue night.

Ed Brale, eighty, thin white hair, a brown waistcoat over a grey shirt, sitting on a low wall by the mill lane and talking with one hand open on his knee. Middle distance: a clay pipe, the lane wall. Background: the village of Tarbeck at evening, mill wheel beyond. Light: low sun on the wall, blue shade behind.

The woman from the river, thirty or so, black hair hanging wet, a slate-grey dress heavy with water, standing on the ford slab with a slate held against her ribs and looking ahead. Middle distance: the black horn comb in her open hand, water running off her hem. Background: the slab ford on the Wen at dusk. Light: low sun going off the water.

The river woman, black hair dripping, a slate-grey wet dress clinging to her arms, looking down at the black horn comb lying open in her flat palm, her fingers deliberately loose. Middle distance: the slate under her other arm, water sheeting off the slab. Background: the ford at low water, dusk. Light: low sun on the wet slab, blue shade behind.

Roon Vail, twenty, dark hair, a scarlet moleskin work coat damp at the shoulders, walking down the mill lane with a lantern held low and his face set. Middle distance: the lantern, a gate post, the lane wall. Background: Tarbeck below him, evening. Light: the lantern flame against the blue dusk.

Foreground: an upturned slate in a wooden frame, one finger resting on its face. Middle: Roon Vail, twenty-six, dark hair, a scarlet moleskin work coat gone shiny at the elbows, bent close over it with a lantern set on the stone beside him. Background: the slab ford on the Wen, dusk. Light: lamp light on the slate, blue dusk behind.

Norea Fenwick, twenty-four, brown hair pinned up, a brown wool shawl over a plain lincoln-green dress, standing at a low garden wall in Tarbeck with her hands still in her shawl and her face turned aside. Middle distance: a shut cottage door, a holly hedge. Background: the mill lane, winter. Light: pale low sun, cold blue shade.

Father Wick, sixty, white hair, a black cope buttoned at the throat, standing on the ford slab at low water with one hand raised in blessing and the hem of his cope in the stream. Middle distance: the black horn comb lying on the stone, the weir beyond. Background: the slab ford, spring afternoon. Light: flat daylight, one warm break on the water.

Tobit Grale, forty, a narrow clean-shaven face, a black coat and a grey stock, standing at the mill door with a large blank sheet of good paper held up in one hand and his thumb on its edge. Middle distance: the mill door frame, a pen case under his arm. Background: Tarbeck mill yard, morning. Light: low sun on the paper.

Mr Dunse, sixty, a grey beard, black coat and white collar, seated at a long plain table with his hands folded on a shut sheet of paper, listening hard. Middle distance: an iron stove with its door ajar, a bench. Background: a plain room in Kelling, winter, shutters closed. Light: stove fire on his face.

Mr Dunse, sixty, a grey beard, a black coat with a white collar, on his feet beside the table with one hand flat on the shut paper, looking levelly across the room. Middle distance: the iron stove, a chair pushed back from the table. Background: the same plain room in Kelling. Light: stove fire low, cold window light.

Tam Fenwick, forty, a broad man with a stubbled jaw, a brown wool coat and a sea-green neckerchief, standing on grey shingle above the water holding a heavy wool sack in both hands. Middle distance: the sack's tied neck, the concrete boat ramp. Background: the open sea off Wrenthorpe, winter noon. Light: hard white noon light, no shade.

The river woman, black hair soaked flat, a slate-grey wet dress to the knee, turned side-on on the slab with the slate held out in both hands, its dark face toward the bank. Middle distance: the black horn comb on the stone, her hem in the water. Background: the ford at dusk, the weir upstream. Light: the last warm band on the water.

The river woman, black hair loose and dripping, a slate-grey dress with the wet hem dark, standing straight on the slab with the slate lifted above her head in one hand, face turned up. Middle distance: the black horn comb on the stone, water at her knees. Background: the ford on the Wen, evening. Light: low sun behind her, cold blue on the slab.

Roon Vail, twenty-eight, dark hair, a scarlet moleskin work coat threadbare at the shoulders, standing alone on the slab with his head bowed and his hands hanging open at his sides. Middle distance: a lantern set on the stone at his feet, the wet slab. Background: the ford on the Wen, the last of the light. Light: dusk going off the water, blue above.

Roon Vail, twenty-nine, dark hair, a scarlet moleskin work coat black at the cuffs, standing at the weir boards in the small hours with a long boat hook in both hands, thinking. Middle distance: the hook's iron head, the boards, the race. Background: the mill wheel dark above, the Wen. Light: one lamp on the boards, hard blue dark.

The river woman, black hair wet, a slate-grey dress dark to the waist, on the slab closing her hand round the black horn comb, her other hand on the slate. Middle distance: a boat hook on the stone, water past the stone. Background: the ford on the Wen, the last evening of March. Light: last light off the water on her hands.

Roon Vail, twenty-nine, dark hair bare, a scarlet moleskin work coat held over one arm, standing in the open mill doorway with one hand on the door frame. Middle distance: a wooden scoop on the bench, a small tin in an open drawer, one plate on the scrubbed table. Background: the mill wheel turning past the window, first light. Light: dawn through the wheel's spokes.
